state_of_play.narrative:
THE WEEK ENDED WITH THE TAPE CALM AND THE POLICY BACKDROP LESS SO. The S&P 500 closed 7,674.37 on 21 August, up 0.43% but down 1.43% on the week; the VIX fell 5.50% to 15.13 after Thursday's spike; the dollar eased a third session to 98.80, down 0.87% on the week, while the 10-year yield rose 4bp to 4.74%. A softer dollar alongside a rising long end is a term-premium move rather than a funding squeeze, and the minutes of the 28-29 July meeting, published 19 August, explain part of it: many participants said tightening would likely be necessary if inflation did not decline, with three regional presidents already dissenting for a 25bp increase at the meeting itself. Markets still price a hold at the 16 September meeting at roughly two-thirds. Jackson Hole runs 27-29 August and Kevin Warsh gives his first keynote as chair on the 28th.

CHINA REOPENED TO NVIDIA'S SECOND-BEST CHIP THREE DAYS BEFORE ITS RESULTS. First H200 shipments reached China in the week to 20 August, with ByteDance and Tencent each taking about 10,000 units - roughly 13% of the 75,000-unit ceiling the January 2026 US licensing framework allows each approved buyer, and the first movement in seven months after Nvidia halted China-bound H200 output in March and redirected that capacity to Vera Rubin. Conditions are still being finalised by China's planning agency and one reported term bundles imported chips with domestic purchases. Nvidia reports fiscal Q2 after the close on 26 August against its own guidance of about $91.0bn plus or minus 2%; secondary previews disagree threefold on the per-share line, so the print will settle its own consensus.

THE MEMORY SUPPLY MAP CHANGED IN CHINA AND THE PRICE MAP CHANGED IN KOREA. YMTC's parent is seeking $4.9bn in a Shanghai listing, which would put a second Chinese memory champion on public markets a month after CXMT raised $8.56bn on the STAR board. Against that, Samsung is reported to have raised foundry prices by up to 15% on demand, to be targeting a further 20% on third-quarter DRAM contract prices and to have taken HBM4 yields to about 80%, while SK hynix is reported to have dropped long-term contract price caps altogether. Nvidia has warned hyperscalers that AI server prices are rising more than 15%. The supply answer and the pricing answer are pointing in opposite directions and both are dated inside the last week.

AUTONOMY CLEARED A REGULATOR AT SCALE AND EUROPE GOT ITS FIRST SERVICE. Nevada's transport regulator unanimously approved three applications on 20 August for paid robotaxi service in Clark County: Tesla up to 5,000 vehicles, Waymo up to 1,000 over twelve months and Uber 1,000 through Motional and Zoox. Taxi and livery groups opposed it on saturation grounds. Separately Uber, Pony.ai and Verne launched the first robotaxi service in Europe with 2,000 vehicles planned. Humanoids went the other way: the industry's own trade body said large-scale humanoid deployment is still years off, and the deployment counts that circulate still have no company disclosure behind them.

THE DEFENCE TRADE IS NOT WHERE ITS ORDER BOOK SAYS IT IS. Rheinmetall's backlog is above EUR 80bn and second-quarter revenue rose about 69% to EUR 3.29bn, yet the shares closed near EUR 1,156 on 20 August - roughly 42% below the EUR 2,007 high set last October and down about a third over twelve months. Bundeswehr documents flag maturity gaps on the Skyranger 30, which has slipped a year, and a Boxer programme running eleven months late; first-half free cash flow was negative EUR 1.6bn. Order intake elsewhere keeps rising - Taiwan has proposed a $35bn defence budget for 2027 and the US Army has asked for 133,000 guided rockets by 2034 - so this is a valuation adjustment rather than a demand one. Late-stage means priced, and this is what priced looks like.

THE POWER CONSTRAINT IS NOW BEING WRITTEN INTO TARIFFS AND INTERCONNECTION RULES. PJM, the largest US grid operator, has proposed curtailing new large data centres first in a shortage and requiring sites above 50MW to bring their own generation; Reuters counted a widening list of jurisdictions restricting data-centre siting; and Morgan Stanley's read is that capital alone no longer clears a site. GE Vernova's gas backlog and slot reservations stand at 116GW against 100GW three months earlier. A constraint that forces developers to bring generation with them is the argument for the equipment, not against it.

AND FOUR AREAS WITH NO LISTED BASKET OF THEIR OWN PRODUCED DATED CATALYSTS IN THE SAME WEEK. A federal appeals court upheld the designation of PFOA and PFOS as hazardous substances on 18 August, leaving polluter-pays liability for PFAS in place and a litigation wave behind it. Saudi Arabia signed $1.16bn of contracts for 8,000MWh of battery storage on 21 August with a $3.6bn second tranche now in bidding. General Fusion has been listed on Nasdaq since 13 July with about $150m of cash, giving fusion a listed pure-play for the first time. And on 19 August Merck and Moderna's individualised cancer vaccine met both endpoints in a 1,137-patient phase 3 melanoma trial - the first positive late-stage readout for an mRNA cancer therapy. All four are on the radar rather than in the treemap: a dated catalyst is a reason to watch, not yet a basket.

Against China refining ~91% of the world's rare earths today, the gap between the target and the base is the whole opportunity.

THE ESCALATION LEG HAS A DATE AND IT IS TOMORROW. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on 20 August that Washington would detail what he called the toughest sanctions in history on Monday 24 August, aimed at Iran's trading partners, as economic pressure replaces military pressure with the war approaching six months. Tehran has already criticised the package as extraterritorial.

AND SO DOES THE DE-ESCALATION LEG, WHICH IS NEW. On 21 August President Masoud Pezeshkian said it is time to end the war while Tehran negotiates from a position of strength, and defended the 17 June memorandum of understanding with Washington against hardline critics in parliament - 'they cannot find even a single clause in this agreement that indicates capitulation'. The 60-day negotiating clock inside that memorandum expired on 17 August; the memorandum itself has not.

WHAT THE PHYSICAL PICTURE SAYS. Brent settled at $94.39 on 21 August, up about 6.4% over two weeks, while the US military says it has escorted more than 660m barrels of crude through the Strait of Hormuz since early May. The chokepoint is functioning and the premium is a risk premium rather than a supply outage.

radar.what: Individualised and computationally designed therapeutics - neoantigen vaccines, AI-designed molecules and the sequencing and manufacturing behind them.
radar.summ: THE FIRST POSITIVE LATE-STAGE READOUT FOR AN INDIVIDUALISED CANCER VACCINE. On 19 August Merck and Moderna reported that the phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial of intismeran autogene with pembrolizumab met its primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival and its key secondary endpoint of distant metastasis-free survival in completely resected stage IIB-IV melanoma, in 1,137 patients randomised two to one. It is the first phase 3 success for both an individualised neoantigen therapy and an mRNA cancer therapy, and the first to beat pembrolizumab alone in the adjuvant setting. The therapy sequences each patient's tumour and encodes up to 34 neoantigens, so the readout validates a manufacturing and computation pipeline rather than a molecule. The cluster moved with it - Moderna rose about 8% and BioNTech about 4% over the following sessions, and Tempus AI added roughly $3bn of value through its stake in a sequencing partner. Against it, Isomorphic Labs has raised $2.1bn and had still not disclosed a clinical candidate as of mid-2026.

Both describe 2026 HBM, DRAM and NAND capacity as essentially sold out; both are running 40-50% operating margins
TrendForce's 9 July release put 3Q26 server DRAM up 13-18% q/q with long-term agreements credited for capping the increase - the cap is the part reported to have gone
signals.assessment: If it holds up against a company source, the one structural brake in view has been removed. It rests on trade press for now and nothing moves on it yet.

signals.headline: Canada sets 8 September for counter-tariffs on $20bn of US goods across six sectors
summary: Carney announced dollar-for-dollar counter-tariffs on $20bn of American products, effective 8 September 2026
Named sectors: steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics
Four outlets carry the $20bn scope on both sides, described as roughly 5% of what Canada ships to the US each year; talks are suspended and none are scheduled
signals.assessment: A threat on Friday now has an effective date, a value and a sector list. Two of the six sectors sit inside themes tracked here.

signals.headline: Bitcoin's best week since 2024 came with about $1.6bn of spot ETF inflows behind it
summary: Bitcoin settled 21 August at $78,335, up 7.26% on the session, with an intraday high near $79,500
Roughly $1.6bn of spot ETF inflows on the week, with BlackRock taking 83% of one $606m inflow day, alongside billions of forced short liquidations and a weaker dollar
It eased to about $77,000 over the weekend with the ETF bid paused
signals.assessment: The flows leg of this case is evidenced for the first time. Set against it, separate coverage describes investors continuing to pull billions while the statute stalls; the two measure different windows and neither is adopted over the other.

signals.headline: The 16 September FOMC carries a ~69% chance of no change and ~31% of a 25bp increase
summary: Polymarket prices the 16 September FOMC at 69% no change / 31% +25bp / ~1.3% cut, read 22 August
CME FedWatch readings give 67.6% HOLD on 13 August and 68.4% HOLD on 20 August, target 3.50-3.75%
The 60.1%/78.8% HIKE figures in circulation are dated 29 July - FOMC day - and fell that afternoon as Warsh spoke
signals.assessment: Instrument readings rather than commentary: Polymarket 69/31 on 22 August, CME FedWatch 67.6% and 68.4% for a hold on 13 and 20 August, target 3.50-3.75%. The 60.1%/78.8% increase readings in circulation are dated 29 July, FOMC day, and fell that afternoon. Friday's tape agrees: equities up, volatility down 5.50%, crypto's best week since 2024.

signals.headline: US-Canada talks collapsed at midnight and 50% Section 338 duties went live on about $20bn of goods
signals.src: NPR / NBC / Bloomberg / Al Jazeera / AP-syndicated
summary: Talks fell apart Friday night minutes before the deadline; duties took effect at the stroke of midnight on hockey sticks, building materials, liquors and certain clothing
USTR Jamieson Greer says Canadian negotiators made eleventh-hour demands that upended a draft deal; a point of contention was Canadian prohibitions on certain US goods and services
Carney suspended negotiations, recalled his team to Ottawa and said Canada 'will match those tariffs dollar for dollar'. No new talks are scheduled
signals.assessment: Duties took effect at 00:01 ET on hockey sticks, building materials, liquors and certain clothing. USTR Jamieson Greer says Canadian negotiators made eleventh-hour demands that upended a draft deal; Carney suspended talks and recalled his team. Four outlets put the scope at $20bn, about 5% of Canadian exports south.

signals.headline: Optical interconnect is up hard on the year: AAOI about +216%, Coherent and Lumentum both doubled
summary: 19 Aug: Coherent +16% to $422, Lumentum +13% through $1,024, Applied Optoelectronics +8%. 12 Aug: LITE +15% on a blowout FQ4, COHR +9%
4 Aug: AAOI +17%, COHR +11%, LITE +6% on a Reuters report of US restrictions on Chinese optical transceivers. Cumulative: AAOI +76% in nine sessions, COHR +48%
NVIDIA's $4bn photonics investment - $2bn each into Lumentum and Coherent - is dated 2 March 2026, not August
signals.assessment: Dated August legs: 4 August AAOI +17%, COHR +10%, LITE +9% on a reported US restriction of Chinese transceivers; 7 August AAOI +13%, COHR +13%, LITE +8% on AAOI's print; 12 August LITE +15%; 19 August COHR +16% and LITE +13%. It cuts both ways - on 10 August COHR fell 12% and LITE 7% on valuation. AAOI guides above $1bn of 2026 sales.

signals.headline: MP Materials ran from about $38 on 29 July to about $60.06 on 21 August, but only 2.26% of it in that final week
summary: MP ~$38 on 29 July to $60.05 on 21 August, +23.5% in the past week; Friday USA Rare Earth +8%, Critical Metals +10%, MP +5%
MP Q2 revenue $108.49m, +89% y/y, beating $95.95m consensus by 13%; Morgan Stanley target to $73, Overweight; Q3 NdPr guided >1,000t at high-$90s/kg; first GM magnet shipments Q4 2026
The G7 agreed at Evian on 17 JUNE 2026 that no single country supply more than 60% of rare-earth and magnet imports by 2030, then 50%
signals.assessment: Q2 revenue $108.49m, up 89% and 12% above a $96.9m consensus; Q3 guidance above 1,000 tonnes of NdPr at realised pricing in the high $90s per kilogram, with Pentagon price support underwriting it. Morgan Stanley raised its target to $73 at overweight; Deutsche Bank and JPMorgan trimmed targets and kept buy ratings.

signals.headline: TrendForce revised its DRAM forecasts up rather than down
summary: 3Q26 PC DRAM contract prices revised UP from +8-13% to +15-20% q/q; 4Q26 from +0-5% to +3-8%
The 9 July release gives 13-18% q/q for SERVER DRAM in 3Q26, with long-term agreements capping increases - this book had cited it as 'conventional DRAM, 13 Aug'
SanDisk FQ4 revenue +371.6% y/y at an 84.6% GAAP gross margin; Western Digital FQ4 +43.8% at a 54.4% non-GAAP gross margin
signals.assessment: Conventional DRAM pricing is being revised UP into end-2026 while CXMT's funded expansion is a 2027 event. The supply fact stands; the near-term shortage is intensifying. Conviction unchanged at 4.

signals.headline: Congress is legislating against the memorandum that opened US Navy shipbuilding to foreign yards
signals.src: USNI News / Navy Times / Defense Daily / Rep. Golden
summary: House FY27 NDAA, passed in July: bars foreign construction of warships AND combat-logistics vessels; no FY27 funds may be obligated for a battle-force ship built abroad
Senate SASC mark strips the Title 10 presidential 'national security interest' waiver, while permitting up to two AUXILIARY ships from foreign yards conditioned on US investment
Hanwha's 'first US Navy contract under MASGA' - an NGLS subcontract with Vard Marine US - is dated 30-31 MARCH 2026, five months before the memorandum
signals.assessment: The House FY27 NDAA, passed in July, bars foreign construction of warships and combat-logistics vessels and blocks FY27 funds for any battle-force ship built abroad. The Senate mark strips the presidential national-security waiver while allowing up to two auxiliaries from foreign yards conditioned on US investment. The White House protested on 24 July.

signals.headline: Record second-quarter central-bank gold buying of 288.9 tonnes, against the weakest half since 2022
signals.src: World Gold Council, Gold Demand Trends Q2 2026
summary: Q2 net central-bank purchases 288.9 tonnes, +62% from 177.9t a year earlier - the highest second quarter on record, bought into a quarter when gold fell ~16%
National Bank of Poland the largest buyer at 51t in Q2 and 82t across H1, toward a self-set ~700t target; PBoC also adding; Turkish and Russian sales slowing
BUT H1 2026 central-bank demand is only ~345 tonnes - the WEAKEST half-year since 2022. The record quarter is catch-up after a very weak Q1
signals.assessment: Confirmed against the World Gold Council's own Gold Demand Trends and corroborated independently: a net 288.9 tonnes in Q2, up 62% year on year, the strongest second quarter on record, bought into a quarter when gold fell about 16%, with Poland the largest buyer at 51 tonnes. The H1 total of about 345 tonnes is the weakest half-year since 2022, so the record quarter is catch-up rather than acceleration.

signals.headline: The $5bn of first-half data-centre electrification orders belongs to GE Vernova
summary: GE Vernova booked ~$5bn of data-centre power equipment orders in H1 2026, more than double its entire 2025 total, with $2.7bn in Q2 alone
Morgan Stanley's 38 GW gap is corroborated across four outlets with a consistent decomposition: ~68 GW of need 2026-28, ~15 GW building, ~15 GW available or contracted
Grid interconnection now takes five to seven years in parts of the US; MS's named fixes include converting former bitcoin-mining sites with existing power
signals.assessment: GE Vernova booked about $5bn of data-centre electrification orders in H1, more than twice full-year 2025, and the split now reconciles arithmetically as $2.4bn in Q1 plus $2.7bn in Q2. The Eaton attribution is not supported.

signals.headline: Nebius expects more than $9bn of customer prepayments in 2026; IREN's $3.4bn NVIDIA deal is dated 7 May
signals.src: Nebius Q2 shareholder letter (SEC 6-K) / IREN IR, GlobeNewswire
summary: Nebius, 12 August: expects over $9bn of customer prepayments in 2026 alongside asset-backed financing, corporate debt and an ATM programme
From the same letter: 'We could sell our entire 2027 capacity on these terms today. We are deliberately not doing so.'
IREN's five-year $3.4bn NVIDIA AI-cloud contract is dated 7 May 2026 - air-cooled Blackwell within ~60MW at Childress, Texas - three and a half months old
signals.assessment: Both were logged and unscored yesterday for want of a date. One is fresh and one is not, and the rule that separated them was applied before either was known to help or hurt.

signals.headline: Iranian oil offers to Chinese buyers fall as the US blockade bites
summary: Sources describe fewer and lower offers reaching Chinese refiners
Brent settled $94.39 on 21 August, up 0.65% and about 6.4% over two weeks
The US Treasury details its sanctions package on Iran's trading partners on Monday 24 August
signals.assessment: The first evidence that the pressure campaign is working on physical flow rather than only on the risk premium. More than 660m barrels have still been escorted through Hormuz since early May, so this remains a premium rather than an outage.

signals.headline: The CFTC begins exploring crypto rules while the CLARITY Act waits for the autumn
summary: The Senate procedural vote on the CLARITY Act ripens 15 September; Polymarket puts 2026 enactment near 15.5% against about 30% a week earlier
Bitcoin's rally topped $79,000 intraday on short covering and ETF inflows before easing
signals.assessment: A regulator writing rules is a narrower and slower route than a statute, but it does not need sixty senators. It is the only forward motion on the legislative leg in a month.

signals.headline: Gold's Friday settle is confirmed at $4,680.60, the highest level of the move
signals.src: COMEX December futures via Yahoo Finance and CNBC quote pages, 21 Aug 2026
summary: A gain of $109.20, or 2.39%, on the session; spot gold is quoted about 1.5% lower near $4,607
Still about 16% below the peak near $5,589-5,602 of 28 January 2026
Central banks bought a net 288.9 tonnes in the second quarter, a record second quarter, against about 345 tonnes for the half - the weakest half since 2022
signals.assessment: The best month since January, and still a recovery rather than a record run. The record quarter of official buying is catch-up after the weakest half in four years.

signals.headline: Saudi Arabia signs $1.16bn of contracts for 8,000MWh of battery storage
signals.src: Saudi Power Procurement Company via Reuters / Zawya / AGBI, 21 Aug 2026
summary: Four storage service agreements worth SAR 4.35bn for 2,000MW over four hours, on a build-own-operate basis
Three 500MW sites go to a Saudi Energy, ACWA Power and Al Sharif consortium; the fourth to ENGIE with a local partner
A second tranche of about 12,000MWh, reported near $3.6bn, has entered bidding
signals.assessment: Storage is being procured as firm capacity under long-dated contracts rather than as an energy-arbitrage asset, which is the change that makes it financeable at this size.

signals.headline: YMTC's parent seeks $4.9bn in a Shanghai listing, a month after CXMT's debut
summary: YMTC is China's leading NAND flash maker; CXMT raised about $8.56bn on the STAR Market on 27 July
A Korean court has separately heard that CXMT planned to use misappropriated Samsung process material
signals.assessment: The supply answer to the memory shortage is being capitalised on public markets. It does not trigger the entry's stated invalidation, which is an average-selling-price rollover, but it funds the thing that eventually would.

signals.headline: Iran's president calls for an end to the war and defends the 17 June memorandum in parliament
signals.src: Al Jazeera / France 24 / Euronews / Gulf News
summary: Masoud Pezeshkian said on 21 August that it is time to end the months-long war while Tehran negotiates from a position of strength
He defended the 17 June 2026 memorandum of understanding with Washington against hardline critics: 'they cannot find even a single clause in this agreement that indicates capitulation'
The 60-day negotiating clock inside that memorandum expired on 17 August; the memorandum itself has not
signals.assessment: The first de-escalation signal in this file for weeks, and it arrives the day after the sanctions warning. The premium now has dated inputs pulling either way.

signals.headline: Quantum's cluster rose hard on 21 August into a year-to-date drawdown
summary: Infleqtion +10%, Rigetti +9-10.5%, IonQ +7% to $44.62 on 21 August
Every established pure play entered that session down on the year: IonQ -7%, Rigetti -27%, D-Wave -28%
IonQ's Q2 was its largest ever - revenue $80.05m, +286.8% y/y, 20.5% above consensus, with FY2026 guidance raised to $280-290m; Rigetti tripled to about $5.1m
signals.assessment: A one-session cluster move inside a year-to-date drawdown is a bounce, not leadership. The revenue leg is now the strong one and the price leg is the weak one - the reverse of how this looked a week ago.

signals.headline: Tesla is reported approved for robotaxi service in Nevada, including Las Vegas
summary: Reported 21 August 2026 by a single enthusiast outlet; no regulator or company source has been found for it
It would follow Waymo running driver-out in Atlanta and clearance to expand across eighteen metropolitan areas
The humanoid side is unchanged: Optimus V3 is described as targeting low-volume Fremont production from summer 2026, consumer availability no earlier than end-2027
signals.assessment: Carried and not treated as a confirmation until a regulator source is found. Autonomy keeps clearing regulators while humanoids keep not clearing evidence.

signals.headline: US authorities say attackers are using AI to target vulnerable water utilities
summary: The warning follows six actively exploited flaws catalogued between 18 and 20 August, including the first AI-lifecycle tool
A VMware vCenter flaw was used by a suspected China-linked group to backdoor 361 victims across 47 countries
signals.assessment: The attack surface is widening in two directions at once - into the AI toolchain and into physical infrastructure - which is what keeps this a spending story rather than a licence-renewal one.

signals.headline: A private-markets manager extends its retail offering into interval funds
signals.src: Business Wire / Alternative Credit Investor, 20-21 Aug 2026
summary: Cox Capital is expanding liquidity solutions for retail investors in private markets
Evergreen structures are spreading in asset-backed finance fundraising, and a US public pension committed to a private capital fund in the same week
signals.assessment: The first dated evidence on the flows leg of this case rather than another valuation datapoint. A route being built is still not measured retail money arriving.

signals.headline: SK hynix publishes a co-packaged optics roadmap, moving beyond memory into interconnect
summary: The roadmap takes a memory maker into the optical interconnect layer of AI infrastructure
An industry forecast puts the AI data-centre optical interconnect market at $144bn by 2030, more than ten times its 2024 size
signals.assessment: The incumbent suppliers' scarcity premium is the case here, and a memory giant entering the layer is the first credible threat to it as well as a confirmation of the demand.

signals.headline: Rheinmetall trades about 42% below last October's high with the backlog above EUR 80bn
summary: Close near EUR 1,156 on 20 August inside a 52-week range of EUR 900.20 to EUR 2,008.00, and down about a third over twelve months
Q2 revenue EUR 3.289bn, up about 69%, with operating profit up 115%; first-half free cash flow was negative EUR 1.6bn
Bundeswehr documents flag maturity gaps: the Skyranger 30 has slipped from mid-2026 to mid-2027 and the Boxer is eleven months behind contract
signals.assessment: A record order book and a share price a third lower is the definition of an opportunity that is largely priced. The demand case is intact; what has been repriced is delivery and cash conversion.

signals.headline: Nevada clears Tesla, Waymo and Uber for up to 7,000 paid robotaxis around Las Vegas
signals.src: TechCrunch / Engadget / Las Vegas Sun, 20-21 Aug 2026
summary: Nevada's transport regulator approved three applications unanimously on 20 August for Clark County
Tesla up to 5,000 vehicles, Waymo up to 1,000 over twelve months, Uber 1,000 through Motional and Zoox
Taxi and livery groups opposed the approvals on market-saturation grounds; reported launch plans start far below the caps
signals.assessment: The first US approval that authorises three competing operators at fleet scale in one market. Authorisation is not deployment, and the gap between the caps and the stated launch plans is where the next twelve months of evidence will come from.

signals.headline: Rocket Lab's $8bn acquisition of Iridium clears antitrust and files with the FCC
signals.src: Rocket Lab investor relations / Via Satellite, 13 and 20 Aug 2026
summary: Announced 29 June: $54 a share in cash and stock, an enterprise value of about $8.0bn
In August the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period lapsed, a Form S-4 was filed and FCC licence-transfer applications were filed on 10 August
Rocket Lab's chief executive says the combined company does not intend to compete directly with Starlink
signals.assessment: It turns a launch and manufacturing business into a vertically integrated operator with its own spectrum and recurring service revenue - a different company from the one the sector's price leg has been tracking.

signals.headline: China lets ByteDance and Tencent import about 10,000 Nvidia H200s each
summary: First H200 shipments reached China in the week to 20 August, the first movement in roughly seven months
The January 2026 US licensing framework allows each of about ten approved Chinese buyers up to 75,000 units, so this is about 13% of the ceiling
China's planning agency is still finalising conditions; one reported term bundles imported chips with domestic purchases, and coverage says most licensed chips must stay in Hong Kong
signals.assessment: It restores a demand channel Nvidia wrote off in March, three days before the print that sets the sector's price - and the volume is small enough that the reopening matters more as a signal about Beijing's stance than as revenue.

signals.headline: The US Treasury will detail its toughest Iran sanctions yet on Monday 24 August
summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on 20 August that Washington would set out what he called the toughest sanctions in history, aimed at Iran's trading partners
The campaign is described as shifting from military to economic pressure as the war nears its six-month mark
Tehran has criticised the package in advance as an assertion of extraterritorial sovereignty
signals.assessment: The energy premium has stopped transmitting into new markets, so it is now tested by whether it holds. Monday is the first of two dated tests.

signals.headline: NuScale closes $8.80 and Oklo $40.87, roughly 79% and 85% below their 2025 peaks
summary: Both fell 5% on 20 August and Centrus fell 6%; peaks were about $57 and $193 in 2025
Q2 revenue: NuScale $75,000 against 365m shares outstanding; Oklo $1.2m with a $48.5m net loss
Uranium spot has been flat near $86/lb since February
signals.assessment: Three cycles without a fresh dated award, and the first in which the cluster price was checked alongside the news. Nuclear conviction goes to 3.

signals.headline: CXMT listed on Shanghai's STAR Market on 27 July and closed its first day up 466%
summary: Raised ~$8.56bn selling 6.688bn shares at CNY 8.66 on Shanghai's STAR Market - Asia's largest IPO of the year - and closed day one at CNY 49, +466%
Became the most valuable company listed on mainland China, passing ICBC; world's fourth-largest DRAM producer at ~7.67% global share in 2025
~350,000 wafer starts a month by end-2026, within 25,000 of Micron's total, with a Shanghai fab 2-3x Hefei reaching volume production in 2027 - and NO HBM project in the prospectus
signals.assessment: It raised about $8.56bn selling 6.688bn shares at CNY 8.66 - Asia's largest listing of the year - closed day one at CNY 49 and became the most valuable company listed on the mainland, passing ICBC. No HBM project appears in the prospectus; named spending goes to wafer lines and process upgrades for DRAM it already makes, at about 350,000 wafer starts a month by end-2026.

signals.headline: Bitcoin leaps past $75,000 and MicroStrategy closes at $112.39
summary: BTC $75,401 on the 21 Aug snapshot, +8.86% and +19.64% on the week - which would be its biggest weekly gain since March 2024
MSTR closed $112.39 on 20 August, +7.81%, after BTC broke $71,000 intraday for the first time since May and forced a wave of short covering
The flag called exit at $91.39 on 14 July with a stated invalidation of BTC >$70k or MSTR >$110. The MSTR leg triggered on a settled close: +23.0% against the call
signals.assessment: Two independent sources put the 20 August close at $112.39, up 7.81% on the session, and a third records a 7.1-8.5% gain. Bitcoin's settled 20 August point is $69,266.19 and it went on to settle 21 August at $78,335.

signals.headline: Long-dated yields rose into the Treasury's buyback announcement rather than falling
summary: The Treasury's expanded buybacks do not begin until 9 September - the relief lasted a single session
Market pricing across sources puts a 16 September hike at roughly 65-80%, on Iran-linked energy costs rather than on growth
signals.assessment: An official bid announced but not yet exercised is a promise, and this session is what the promise was worth.

signals.headline: The UAE suspends all trade and financial transactions with Iran after two ballistic missiles
summary: Two ballistic missiles were fired from Iran toward the UAE on 18-19 August, one landing in its territorial waters; the UAE defence ministry assessed both as targeting maritime traffic
The UAE had been a major trading partner for a sanctioned Iran; Tehran categorically denies launching them
Brent settled 20 August at $93.78, +2.36% on the day and +5.61% on the week
signals.assessment: The UAE suspended all trade, commercial exchange and financial transactions with Iran on 19 August after two ballistic missiles landed on its territory. The regional counterweight to the sanctions campaign narrows further.

signals.headline: Walmart falls ~9% on missed US comps - its worst day in four years - while banking ~$2.9bn of tariff refunds
summary: Adjusted EPS $0.81 on revenue of $187.9bn, +19.1% and +5.9% y/y, with the gross margin rate at 25.4% helped by the refund
Eligible for roughly $2.9bn of IEEPA tariff refunds and says it will spend them cutting prices in Q3
US comparable sales missed and the adjusted-earnings path for Q3 and the full year was judged short; the stock fell about 9%, taking 703.84 points off the Dow
signals.assessment: The second retailer in three sessions whose headline was flattered by a refund the Supreme Court handed it in February. Target beat on the same mechanism; Walmart missed on the business.

signals.headline: Micron's fiscal Q3 did $41.46bn of revenue with about $100bn of remaining performance obligation
summary: Reported 24 June 2026: revenue $41.46bn (+346% y/y, +74% q/q), gross margin 84.9%, EPS $25.11, operating cash flow $25.39bn
DRAM revenue $31.3bn (76% of total, +343% y/y); data-centre revenue above $25bn, an annualised run rate over $100bn; Q4 guided to ~$50bn at ~86% margin
About $100bn of remaining performance obligation under strategic customer agreements
signals.assessment: Logged as not-adopted on 20 August from a single aggregator with an extreme figure. The re-check was scheduled, run, and it was right. Withholding was correct; so was going back.

signals.headline: A 38 GW gap in US data-centre power to 2028; GE Vernova's gas backlog goes 100 GW to 116 GW
signals.src: Motley Fool / GE Vernova IR / Utility Dive
summary: Morgan Stanley estimate carried 20 August: ~68 GW of US data-centre need across 2026-28, ~15 GW under construction and ~15 GW available or contracted
GE Vernova Q2 2026: gas equipment backlog plus slot reservations 100 GW -> 116 GW, guided to at least 125 GW under contract by year-end, on 20 GW signed in the quarter
Tesla's Megablock - four Megapacks around one transformer, 20 MWh a block - ships H2 2026 from a Brookshire, Texas plant targeting 50 GWh a year
signals.assessment: The AI-power quiet window ends on quantification rather than on a contract. One syndicated line attributing $5bn of orders to Eaton is contested and not used.

signals.headline: The KOSPI's break is reversed - up 5.89% to 6,853 on 20 August
summary: Reverses the 5.55% fall to 6,488.24 of 19 August almost exactly; Samsung up over 4% and SK hynix over 7%
Korea remains roughly 27% below the 9,385.59 record it set in June - the drawdown is not repaired, but the break is closed
Chip shipments reported at ~$26bn in the first twenty days of August, nearly triple the year-ago figure (one source, logged with a re-check)
signals.assessment: The index then rose 0.88% to 6,912.95 on 21 August, a second consecutive gain, and the arithmetic checks: 6,853 + 60.37 = 6,912.95. Korea remains about 26% below its June record of 9,385.59.

signals.headline: CLARITY Act enactment odds halve even as the White House pushes it, to about 15.5% from about 30%
summary: Galaxy Research separately cut its odds of 2026 enactment from 50% to 30%
15 September is a FIRST PROCEDURAL VOTE at 2:15pm ET, not final passage; 60 votes are needed against 53 Republicans
The unresolved issue is ethics language preventing senior officials, including the President, from profiting from crypto
signals.assessment: Polymarket's 2026 enactment odds fell to about 15.5% from roughly 30% a week earlier and Galaxy Research cut its own estimate from 50% to 30%. The Senate has since pushed the bill to the autumn, with the procedural vote ripening 15 September.

signals.headline: The Supreme Court's 401(k) alternatives case is Anderson v. Intel, No. 25-498, cert granted 16 January
summary: Intel 401(k) participants challenged the inclusion of private equity, hedge funds and other alternatives on fee and underperformance grounds
Question presented: whether pleading an ERISA fiduciary-breach claim predicated on underperformance requires alleging a 'meaningful benchmark'
The DOL's companion safe-harbour proposal was published in the Federal Register on 31 March 2026; comments closed 1 June. The argument date is still not pinned
signals.assessment: Set for the October Term 2026. The Court has not yet published its argument calendar, so no argument date exists to cite. It is the legal spine of the private-markets case: whether plan fiduciaries face suit for including alternatives.

signals.headline: The Section 338 pause on Canadian goods expires at 00:01 ET on 22 August
signals.src: GHY International / Holland & Knight / PM of Canada
summary: The duties cover roughly $20bn of Canadian imports - specifically dairy, alcoholic beverages and motor vehicles - under proclamations dated 20 July 2026
Carney says Canada 'stands ready to engage intensively'; USTR Greer confirms talks have not been cut off
Section 232 is unaffected: 50% on articles wholly of steel, aluminium or copper and 25% on derivatives, on full customs value, running to 31 December 2027
signals.assessment: The pause expired with no deal and the duties took effect. Naming it as a deadline rather than an outcome was what the calendar supported at the time.

signals.headline: CISA adds an actively exploited PAN-OS flaw to KEV - Unit 42 says exploitation began 17 May
summary: CVE-2026-0257, CVSS 7.8 - lets an attacker bypass restrictions and establish VPN connections to vulnerable appliances via GlobalProtect
Exploited for weeks before it was known; KEV listing requires federal agencies to patch rapidly
Microsoft's August 2026 Patch Tuesday addressed 415 vulnerabilities, including one exploited zero-day, three disclosed zero-days and 62 critical
signals.assessment: Demand evidence for the category and a two-way risk for the named vendor, which reports on 1 September. CrowdStrike reports 26 August.

signals.headline: SMR equities fall 5-6% on rate anxiety alone; uranium spot flat since February
signals.src: 24/7 Wall St. / Cameco / ANS Nuclear Newswire
summary: NuScale -5% to $8.80, Oklo -5% to $40.87, Centrus Energy -6% to $172.68 on 20 August
NuScale's Q2 2026 revenue was $75,000 against a share count up to 365 million
Cameco's end-July spot was $86.36/lb, roughly unchanged since February, with futures at $86.60 - nowhere near the sub-$80 kill condition
signals.assessment: The quiet window broke negatively. The case rests on AI power demand and is intact; six months without price leadership is a failed first signal.

signals.headline: Bitcoin tops $69,000 for the first time since June; ~$1.44bn of shorts liquidated
summary: BTC $69,381 on the 20 August fetch (+7.27%), after roughly $1.44bn of short positions were liquidated
Drivers cited are macro rather than crypto-native: the Treasury buyback expansion, a bond rally and a softer dollar
Trump publicly urged Congress to advance crypto market-structure legislation; an SEC crypto proposal is also cited
signals.assessment: Raises the crypto theme 2 to 3, and puts the MSTR exit flag's stated invalidation (BTC above $70k) within 0.9%.

signals.headline: China leaves loan prime rates unchanged for a 15th consecutive month
summary: The 20 August fixing left the one-year at 3.00% and the five-year-plus at 3.50%
The seven-day reverse repo has also been on hold for 15 months since its May 2025 cut, so the pricing basis did not move
Third consecutive observed absence of policy against the July activity miss
signals.assessment: The ammunition remains available and unspent. For a policy-driven economy, a third straight non-response is itself the signal.

signals.headline: Japan will build its first large shipbuilding dock since 2017 and Belfast's cranes return
summary: Japan is to construct its first large shipbuilding dock in nine years
Harland & Wolff's Belfast cranes are getting a GBP 3m overhaul ahead of a major contract after twenty years out of use
Finland selected Helsinki Shipyard for a next-generation icebreaker on 21 August
signals.assessment: Allied yard capacity is being rebuilt with real capital while the US rule that would let those yards build American warships is being legislated against. The capacity is the durable half.

signals.headline: TerraPower's reactor carries thermal storage that lets output follow a data centre's load
summary: The sodium-cooled design stores heat, so electrical output can be varied without varying the reactor
OpenAI separately announced a large Ohio data centre with an Nvidia guarantee on 17 August
signals.assessment: Load-following is the specific attribute a data-centre buyer needs and that conventional nuclear does not offer. It is a design claim, not an order, and the listed cluster is still 79-85% below its 2025 peaks.

signals.headline: July minutes show many Fed officials would raise rates if inflation does not fall
signals.src: FOMC minutes of 28-29 July, released 19 Aug 2026
summary: Many participants judged that policy tightening would likely be necessary if inflation did not decline
Three regional presidents dissented in favour of a 25bp increase at the meeting itself, citing broad-based price pressures
Participants expected inflation to slow but flagged elevated uncertainty on inflation, the labour market and growth
signals.assessment: The committee is more hawkish than the pricing. Markets still put the 16 September meeting at about two-thirds a hold, and Jackson Hole on 27-29 August sits between the two.

signals.headline: Merck and Moderna's individualised cancer vaccine meets both endpoints in phase 3
signals.src: Merck press release / Fierce Biotech, 19 Aug 2026
summary: The INTerpath-001 trial of intismeran autogene plus pembrolizumab met recurrence-free survival and distant metastasis-free survival in resected stage IIB-IV melanoma
1,137 patients randomised two to one; the therapy sequences each tumour and encodes up to 34 patient-specific neoantigens
The first positive phase 3 for both an individualised neoantigen therapy and an mRNA cancer therapy, and the first to beat pembrolizumab alone in this setting
signals.assessment: It validates a manufacturing and computation pipeline rather than a single molecule, which is what makes it a sector event rather than a drug event.

signals.headline: Samsung raises chipmaking prices by up to 15% as demand outruns capacity
summary: Foundry price increases of up to 15% reported by sources
Nvidia has separately warned hyperscalers that AI server prices are rising by more than 15%
Chip-equipment lead times are reported out to 24 months
signals.assessment: Pricing power is moving down the stack from memory into foundry and up into finished servers, which is what a genuine capacity shortage looks like rather than a demand narrative.

signals.headline: Rheinmetall books a DKK 745m Danish MASS decoy award alongside a >EUR 500m Bundeswehr order
signals.src: Danish defence procurement agency via ad-hoc-news
summary: The Danish award, about $116m, covers Multi Ammunition Softkill Systems for Absalon and Iver Huitfeldt class frigates
Both contracts are dated 19 August and both now carry a second source
Backlog above EUR 80bn after EUR 11.37bn of new business, on Q2 revenue of EUR 3.29bn and earnings of EUR 124m
signals.assessment: Two of the three contracts that rested on one aggregator are corroborated. The EUR 3.4bn Italian heavy-tank programme still does not.

signals.headline: Lincoln Educational Services opens a 26th campus in Tempe while UTI trades sharply lower
summary: Announced 19 August: a first Arizona campus of about 90,000 square feet in north Tempe, Lincoln's 26th
Universal Technical Institute cut FY26 revenue guidance to $893-900m from $905-915m and net income to $32-36m from $40-45m
Lincoln trades far above its start-of-year level while UTI trades sharply below; both figures are undated snapshots and neither is pinned
signals.assessment: A cluster moving in opposite directions is two companies rather than a theme with a tailwind. The skilled-trades card moves from fading to stalled on it.

signals.headline: Treasury at least doubles long-dated bond buybacks; 10-year falls to 4.65%
summary: Announced 19 August: the cap on liquidity-support buybacks of longer-dated coupons rises from $2bn to at least $4bn per operation
Targets the 10-20 and 20-30 year sectors where dealer demand had thinned; operations run 9 September to early November
It repurchases off-the-run paper to cure dislocation - it does not finance new spending
signals.assessment: The Treasury will at least double liquidity-support buybacks of longer-dated nominal coupons, from a $2bn cap to at least $4bn per operation across the 10-20 and 20-30 year sectors, running 9 September into early November. It buys off-the-run paper to cure dislocation and does not finance new spending.

signals.headline: The 50% Section 338 duties on Canada were paused for three days, to 22 August
summary: Trump paused the duties for three days, to 22 August, less than two hours before the 00:01 ET deadline
Carney confirmed the suspension and said substantial progress had been made but important work remains
This page said on 19 August that the duties were in force. They were not.
signals.assessment: Paused less than two hours before the 19 August deadline. They took effect at 00:01 ET on 22 August when talks collapsed.

signals.headline: SK hynix approves a KRW 40tn (~$28.6bn) buyback and full share cancellation
summary: Board resolution 19 August: the largest treasury cancellation ever initiated by a listed South Korean company
~24.07m shares, about 3.3% of the 730,492,365 outstanding; buying starts 20 August and runs about three months
Shareholder-return target raised to over half of cumulative 2025-27 free cash flow, pulling forward a November 2024 programme
signals.assessment: The strongest evidence yet for 'shortage, not cycle'. A management team answering a 9% fall with a record cancellation is making a claim about the cycle's length.

signals.headline: Nebius launches a $4.5bn convertible bond offering and falls 13.7%
summary: Announced 19 August: $2.75bn due 2030 and $1.75bn due 2034, with $375m and $300m upsize options
Alongside it, exchanges of a portion of its 2.00% 2029s and 3.00% 2031s into Class A shares
Proceeds fund data-centre construction, GPU procurement and the AI cloud platform; CoreWeave fell 4% in sympathy, both rebounded
signals.assessment: The neocloud entry's stated invalidation tested in the primary market. The capital is available and it is being paid for in dilution rather than in spread.

signals.headline: Target's profit doubles on $752m of tariff refunds; full-year guidance raised
summary: Q2 included $994m of pretax tariff-refund benefit, $752m net and $1.65 of EPS, following the Supreme Court's IEEPA ruling
Net sales +5.3%, comparable sales +3.8% on 3.6% higher comparable traffic; digital comps +8.7%
GAAP and adjusted EPS guidance raised to $9.90-$10.90 from $7.50-$8.50
signals.assessment: The consumer is holding for a second session running - but $1.65 of the EPS is a tariff refund, not trading, and the headline overstates it.

signals.headline: The US reviews Chinese firms' offshore access to Nvidia chips after a Thai data-centre route
summary: Chinese firms have reached GB300 compute through data centres in Southeast Asia despite the shipment ban
A White House official named Moonshot AI as having used a facility in Thailand, days after its July model release
The current regime controls physical chips but not remote access; a key agency is now reviewing that gap
signals.assessment: Extends the 15 August BIS D:5 action from ownership to access. Closing it would reach the rental layer as much as the chip layer.

signals.headline: KOSPI falls 5.55% to 6,488 and triggers a sidecar; Nikkei -3.23%
summary: A sell-side sidecar suspended program selling as KOSPI 200 futures fell more than 5%
SK hynix -9%, Samsung -7%, Kioxia -10%, SoftBank -6%; the 10-year JGB reached its highest since 1996
The KOSPI is now roughly 31% below the 9,385.59 record it set in June 2026
signals.assessment: The KOSPI fell 5.55% to 6,488.24 on 19 August and triggered a sell-side sidecar, with SK hynix -9%, Samsung -7% and Kioxia -10%; the Nikkei fell 3.23% and the 10-year JGB reached its highest since 1996.

signals.headline: UK July CPI 2.9%, a four-month high
summary: Released 19 August; up from 2.6% in June and above May and April's 2.8%
The first G7 consumer-price print to carry the Hormuz energy pass-through
It arrives after the gilt and Treasury long ends had already repriced, not before
signals.assessment: Converts the energy-premium entry's forecast leg into a print. BoE held Bank Rate at 3.75% on 30 July.

signals.headline: 50% Section 338 duties on Canadian goods are now in force
summary: Effective 00:01 ET on 19 August on motor vehicles, alcoholic beverages and dairy; ~$20bn of annual imports
No exemption for USMCA-qualifying goods; the first modern use of the 1930 statute
PM Carney has not retaliated and says Canada is open to talks; Ontario's Ford is pushing for a matching response
signals.assessment: The tariff architecture widening in instrument rather than in rate. Canada's response is the near-term variable.

signals.headline: China's loan prime rates unchanged for a 14th month; still no answer to the July miss
summary: One-year LPR 3.00% and five-year 3.50%, unchanged at record lows; the August fixing is due 20 August
The RRR and the policy rate both remain available and unspent after a 50bp RRR cut in May
A search result describing a large August 2026 PBoC stimulus package was checked and rejected - it is the September 2024 package resurfacing
signals.assessment: An observed absence of policy, which for a policy-driven economy is itself the signal. Second consecutive cycle.

signals.headline: General Fusion gives its first update as a listed company, with plasma at 8.4 million degrees
summary: Listed on Nasdaq as GFUZ since 13 July 2026 with about $150m of cash, giving fusion a listed pure-play for the first time
LM26 compressed plasma with a lithium liner to about 0.72 keV; the next targets are 1 keV, then 10 keV and the Lawson criterion
The cash is stated to fund planned milestones through the end of 2028
signals.assessment: A temperature milestone is not a net-energy milestone, and one pre-revenue listing is not a basket. What has changed is that the domain is now observable in public markets at all.

signals.headline: A federal appeals court upholds the hazardous-substance designation of PFOA and PFOS
signals.src: D.C. Circuit, Chamber of Commerce v. EPA, No. 24-1193, 18 Aug 2026
summary: The court denied the industry petitions and left EPA's 2024 Superfund designation in place
It interpreted the statute independently rather than deferring to the agency, and rejected the nondelegation and vagueness arguments
Veolia has sued alleged polluters in Delaware to recover treatment costs and a Delaware supplier has sued nine companies
signals.assessment: Polluter-pays liability for PFAS is now durable and the route to designating further compounds is open. The spending it forces is municipal and industrial rather than discretionary.

signals.headline: CISA catalogues an actively exploited MLflow flaw - the first AI-lifecycle tool in the catalogue
summary: CVE-2026-64849, a server-side request forgery in MLflow, added 19 August on evidence of active exploitation
The 18 August batch added four more: Microsoft IKE service extensions, SharePoint, Broadcom VMware vCenter and Apple macOS
The vCenter path-traversal flaw was used by a suspected China-linked group to plant a backdoor across 361 victim addresses in 47 countries
signals.assessment: The machine-learning tool chain is now itself an exploited attack surface. That is a widening of the cyber surface rather than another vulnerability count.

signals.headline: WSJ: nine big-tech firms carry ~$3tn of off-balance-sheet AI commitments
signals.src: Wall Street Journal (via TipRanks / Asharq Al-Awsat / CryptoBriefing)
summary: Published 18 August; roughly five times the ~$600bn of capex the same firms reported over the trailing twelve months
Split ~$0.9-1.2tn of unstarted data-centre leases and ~$1.5-1.9tn of purchase commitments for chips, construction and energy
Alphabet $811bn; Meta ~$420bn, close to three times its reported debt
signals.assessment: The sharpest form yet of the master factor's own invalidation. Not spread stress - a disclosure finding, arriving as the long end reprices the cost of carrying it.

signals.headline: OpenAI Q2 revenue $6.7bn (+18% q/q) with widening losses; Anthropic roughly doubles to $11.6bn
summary: OpenAI grew 18% sequentially from $5.7bn in Q1 and pushed its profit target further out
Anthropic's revenue more than doubled sequentially to $11.6bn with a small operating profit
The first quarter the frontier-lab revenue league table has changed hands
signals.assessment: Demand concentration, not demand collapse - but one of the two buyers underwriting the capex slowed, which is what the hardware tape reacted to.

signals.headline: Memory and semis sell off hard: SOX -5.4%, Micron -5%, Western Digital -7%
summary: SanDisk -6% to $1,681.10, Micron -5% to $962.85, Western Digital -7% to $500.05 on 18 August
Coverage attributes it to rising Treasury yields and positioning, not company news - SanDisk was +44% on the week and +653% YTD into it
The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 5.4%, shedding more than $680bn of market value
signals.assessment: A rate and positioning reset in the most crowded corner of AI hardware. The stated invalidation is an ASP rollover, and contract ASPs are still forecast up.

signals.headline: Home Depot beats and reaffirms guidance in 'frozen housing market conditions'
summary: Beat on both revenue and EPS on 18 August and reaffirmed full-year guidance
CFO Richard McPhail described the customer as 'a healthy cohort' who has not returned to big projects
Reported under an interim office of the chief executive after Ted Decker's medical leave, announced 12 August
signals.assessment: Weak housing, not a weak consumer. It cuts against the labour-turn entry rather than for it. Target reports 19 Aug, Walmart 20 Aug.

signals.headline: Japan's dysprosium imports fell 82% in the first half under China's export curbs
summary: Dysprosium is a heavy rare earth used in high-temperature magnets for motors and defence systems
China has separately slowed exports of key optical and aerospace metals to Taiwan (Nikkei, 20 August)
signals.assessment: This is the first hard trade-data measurement that the export curbs bind rather than merely threaten. It is also the strongest argument yet for the non-Chinese processing capacity the theme is built on.

signals.headline: The largest US grid operator proposes cutting power to new data centres first in a shortage
signals.src: PJM proposal via Tom's Hardware / Reuters, 17-18 Aug 2026
summary: PJM would curtail new large loads ahead of other customers during capacity shortages
Sites above 50MW would be required to bring their own generation
Reuters separately mapped a widening set of jurisdictions restricting data-centre siting
signals.assessment: A rule that forces new load to arrive with its own generation attached is an argument for turbines, switchgear and on-site storage rather than against the build.

signals.headline: US-Iran 60-day deadline expires with no deal and no extension
summary: The 60-day window set in a June memorandum lapsed on 17 August, deadlocked on Hormuz and on frozen Iranian funds
Neither side would extend it, and Iran does not consider the clock to have started
Washington has now turned on Oman, the channel through which the Hormuz-management talks were running
signals.assessment: The negotiated route has lapsed rather than stalled. This is the energy-premium theme's driver hardening, not easing.

signals.headline: US 30-year Treasury yield reaches 5.31%, the highest since 2007
summary: Heavy issuance plus tariff and energy inflation drove the long bond to a 19-year high on 17 August
The UK 30-year gilt sat near 5.77% the same day, with the 10-year back above 5%
Yesterday this desk called the gilt move a UK-specific transmission - both G7 long ends moved together
signals.assessment: The 30-year reached 5.31% on 17 August, its highest since 2007, the same day the UK gilt curve moved - so the energy-premium transmission is not UK-specific.

signals.headline: China's July activity misses across the board; still no policy answer
summary: Industrial output +4.5% y/y vs 4.8% expected; retail sales +0.6% vs 1.5% expected
Fixed-asset investment -6.7% year-to-date; urban unemployment up to 5.2%
As of 18 August the PBoC has not responded - policy shifted to a data-dependent hold in 1H26 after a 50bp RRR cut in May
signals.assessment: The easing ammunition exists and is unspent. Absence of a response is itself the finding this run.

signals.headline: Rheinmetall cuts 2026 sales guidance after Berlin scraps the F126 frigate programme
summary: Guidance cut in mid-August to EUR 13.7-14.2bn from EUR 14.0-14.5bn, a EUR 300m hit to the naval division
Germany pulled the EUR 12.8bn F126 programme in early July after spending EUR 2.3bn, pivoting to eight MEKO A-200 frigates from ThyssenKrupp
Rheinmetall suspended plans to hire 1,000 naval staff but held its EUR 5bn 2030 naval revenue target
signals.assessment: Confirms the entry's UK-primes-vs-EU-laggard split rather than breaking it. A lost domestic competition is not a budget cut.

signals.headline: Q2 13Fs: SpaceX and Alphabet bought, NVIDIA and Broadcom sold
summary: All nine institutions disclosing a SpaceX position added to or increased it; Alphabet drew 11 buyers including Berkshire
NVIDIA and Broadcom saw net selling; CoreWeave and Seagate gained momentum
Situational Awareness LP filed on 14 August and is characterised as peak AI concentration ahead of an unwind - its reported AUM and return figures come from a secondary aggregator and are NOT adopted
signals.assessment: Divided, and rotating rather than adding. The 17 Aug put-book trace re-enters here as new evidence after being formally retired on 18 Aug.

signals.headline: Fluence starts construction on a 400 MWh German grid battery and signs two hyperscaler MSAs
summary: Fluence and LEAG began building the Heinersbrueck GridBattery on 14 August - their second joint project
Master supply agreements signed with two major hyperscale datacentres; datacentre pipeline +30% since Q1 at ~12 GWh contracted
Base Power raised $1bn on 3 August for a US-manufactured battery platform
signals.assessment: Storage is the AI-power leg that delivers inside this cycle, and it is now shipping in Europe as well as the US.

signals.headline: US opens Navy shipbuilding to foreign yards; Hanwha Ocean +5.6%, Fincantieri also higher
summary: National-security memorandum signed 14 August (this desk previously dated it 15 August)
Covers surface combatants, consolidated cargo replenishment tankers and roll-on/roll-off vessels
Every vessel after the first two must be built in the US, with possible technology transfer attached
signals.assessment: A second listed price response widens the basket beyond Korea. Still 4 of 5 - flows are the missing criterion.

signals.headline: TrendForce sees conventional DRAM contract prices +13-18% q/q, NAND +10-15%
summary: Published 13 August; HBM4 costs $31-32/GB against HBM3E at $17-18/GB
Samsung's entire 2026 HBM capacity is sold out; HBM4 yields reported near 80%
SK hynix holds 50-55% of the HBM market
signals.assessment: Third independent supply-side confirmation in a fortnight. The shortage-not-cycle framing keeps getting better evidenced.

signals.headline: CoreWeave's Q2 revenue doubles to $2.6bn and Nebius grows 514%; both jump on the print
summary: CoreWeave revenue $2.6bn, up 112% from $1.2bn, shares +19% on 12 August; a $104bn backlog against a $58.8bn market value
Nebius revenue up 514% to $575m with the value of contracts won quadrupling, shares +34%
Nebius funds 50-60% of the capital spending tied to major contracts from customer prepayments; CoreWeave carries more than $35bn of debt
signals.assessment: The recipients converted. The open question is no longer whether demand is real but which balance sheet survives funding the next round of it.

signals.headline: Prediction markets take two regulatory hits: Kalshi restrained in Washington, Polymarket debanked
summary: A judge ordered Kalshi to stop offering most wagers in Washington state on 12 August
JPMorgan debanked Polymarket on regulatory concerns on 13 August
Kalshi spent $500,000 lobbying federal policymakers in Q2 2026, more than in any prior quarter
signals.assessment: The regulatory risk this desk logged as a caveat on 18 Aug has converted into a court order and a banking-access problem. The leg is weaker, not stronger.

signals.headline: Roundhill lists the first-ever Photonics & Optics ETF (LYTE) and Neocloud ETF (NCLD)
summary: Both listed 6 August 2026 at a 0.65% gross expense ratio
LYTE: 12 holdings on ~$72m of first-day volume - Lumentum 15.4%, Coherent 15.2%, NewLink 14.6%, ZTE 14.2%, Tianfu 7.9%
NCLD: ~20 holdings, actively managed, targeting GPU-as-a-service and AI data centres
signals.assessment: Closes signal 2 of the 5-signal check for optics for the first time - and corrects this page's own claim that neither fund existed.

signals.headline: SpaceX's first published quarter: revenue $7.81bn, up 92%, with Starlink at 12 million subscribers
summary: For the quarter ended 30 June and released 4 August: revenue $7.81bn against a $6.9bn S&P Visible Alpha estimate
Connectivity, which is Starlink, $4.29bn (+66%) on 12 million subscribers, double a year earlier; an xAI and Grok line at $2.56bn (+247%)
Net loss narrowed to $541m from about $1bn; CFO Bret Johnsen guided to $100bn of annualised recurring revenue by year-end and Elon Musk moved his $1tn revenue target from 2031 to 2030
signals.assessment: The shares fell on AI spending rather than on the top line - the payer-versus-recipient question running inside a single company. Space moves from emerging to building on it.

signals.headline: The Nasdaq-100 added CoreWeave, Nebius and Astera Labs in June, not August
summary: Announced 11 June, effective before the open on Monday 22 June 2026
Rocket Lab and Teradyne joined in the same rebalance; Charter, Cognizant, Insmed, Verisk and Zscaler were removed
This page credited the inclusion on 19 August as the neocloud theme's first hard flows evidence
signals.assessment: A two-month-old event presented as this month's confirmation. It also hands the space theme a flows fact and the cyber theme a small outflow, neither of which this book had.

signals.headline: Quantinuum listed on Nasdaq in June, raising $1.68bn - a basket member this book had missed
summary: IPO'd 4 June 2026 at $60 a share under the ticker QNT; ~$12.7bn valuation at filing; closed flat on debut
2025 revenue $30.9m (from $23m) with a $192.6m net loss; Honeywell and Cambridge Quantum retain ~82%
The quantum radar entry's expression line had listed only IONQ, RGTI, QBTS and IBM
signals.assessment: A coverage gap of this desk's own, closed. It widens the basket but does not confirm flows - a flat debut is not a demand signal, so the score stays 4 of 5.

signals.headline: Fincantieri's $30m landing-ship award is dated 15 April
summary: Awarded 15 April 2026 for materials procurement and engineering on the first four Medium Landing Ship hulls
It follows a February 2026 Navy RFP for a programme that could reach 35 ships
It predates the 14 August national-security memorandum entirely
signals.assessment: The shipbuilding radar entry's only award turns out not to be evidence the memorandum produced anything. Score cut to 3 of 5.

signals.headline: The Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs 6-3 on 20 February
summary: Roberts, 6-3: IEEPA's power to 'regulate importation' does not include the power to impose tariffs, which is a branch of the taxing power reserved to Congress
All IEEPA tariffs terminated at 00:00 ET on 24 February; Section 122 also fell, expiring 24 July
The weighted average applied US tariff rate went from 14.9% to 8.2%; ~$128.68bn of refunds had been accepted for processing by 31 July
signals.assessment: This book had never recorded it, while carrying reshoring-by-tariff at conviction 5. Section 232 and Section 301 survive intact; the driver is cut to 3.

what_changed.line: Contract prices lost their cap while China took a second memory champion to public markets.
Best week since 2024 on $1.6bn of ETF inflows, while the statute slipped and a regulator stepped in.
Beijing let the H200 back in at about a tenth of the permitted volume, three days before the print.
The biggest US grid operator would curtail new data centres first and make them bring generation.
Attackers are now using AI against water utilities, days after the first AI tool entered the exploited list.
A load-following reactor design is the demand-side answer; the listed cluster is still 79-85% off its peaks.
A memory giant published a co-packaged optics roadmap, into a market forecast at $144bn by 2030.
Japan's dysprosium imports fell 82%, the first hard measurement that China's curbs bind.
Allied yard capacity is being rebuilt in Japan and Belfast while the US access rule is contested.
Friday's settle confirmed at $4,680.60, the best month since January and still 16% below the record.
Revenue converted at both recipients; the open question is which balance sheet funds the next round.
Nevada authorised three operators and up to 7,000 paid robotaxis; humanoids went backwards on evidence.
The retail-access leg got its first dated item: a manager extending into interval funds.
A record order book and a share price about 42% below last October's high.
Saudi Arabia bought 8,000MWh of batteries for $1.16bn, with a larger second tranche in tender.
The sector's biggest listed name cleared antitrust on an $8bn move into satellite services.
The first individualised cancer vaccine to succeed in phase 3, and the cluster moved with it.
Fusion has a listed pure-play for the first time, and it reported plasma at 8.4 million degrees.
A federal appeals court left polluter-pays liability for PFAS in place, and the lawsuits are running.
Iranian barrels are finding fewer Chinese buyers, days before the sanctions package lands.
